ev.chn_m_lantern.text: At the Lantern Festival the whole town glows: fish lanterns, lotus lanterns, lanterns hung with riddles. You solved one and won a sweet rice ball for your trouble.
ev.chn_m_new_year.text: On New Year’s night firecrackers bang in the street - bamboo tubes packed with gunpowder. Fresh door-god pictures guard the gate, and in the morning, in a new jacket, you bow to your elders and get coppers on a red string.
ev.chn_m_qingming.text: At the Qingming festival the whole clan goes out to the ancestors’ graves: you pull the weeds, set out food and burn paper money for the other world. Then, as custom demands, you stroll over the spring hills.
ev.chn_m_dragon_boat.text: On the Double Fifth, dragon boats race down the river, drums pounding and rowers roaring. You ate so many zongzi - rice wrapped in bamboo leaves - that you barely made it home.
ev.chn_m_mid_autumn.text: On the Mid-Autumn night everyone watches the full moon. There are round cakes and pears on the table, and the old folk tell of the white hare on the moon pounding the elixir of immortality.
ev.chn_m_teahouse.text: In the teahouse by the bridge, landscape scrolls hang on the walls, a waiter shouts orders to the kitchen, and at the next table people argue about rice prices and the latest edict. You stayed half the day.
ev.chn_m_west_lake.text: On a summer evening you took a boat out on the West Lake. Willows along the Su Causeway, lotus flowers, a flute playing on a neighbouring boat - it seems too beautiful to be real.
ev.chn_m_night_market.text: Kaifeng’s night market roars on past the third watch: roast mutton, honey cakes, conjurers and fortune-tellers. You came home near dawn with sticky fingers and an empty purse.
ev.chn_m_foreigners.text: At the harbour you saw bearded men in white turbans - merchants from the land of the Dashi, as the Arabs are called here. They haggle through an interpreter and count our copper coins faster than the money-changers.
ev.chn_m_jiaozi.text: At the market someone paid for a sack of salt with a slip of paper covered in red seals - a jiaozi. Strange to hold money that weighs nothing: the same salt in iron coins would be a load to carry on your back.
ev.chn_m_pepper.text: The cook at the eating house throws a generous handful of red Sichuan peppercorns into the pot. The first spoonful numbed your lips, the second brought tears, and the third felt wonderful.
ev.chn_m_kang.text: In winter the wind carries yellow dust mixed with snow. The whole household sleeps on the kang - a warm brick platform with embers smouldering underneath. Whoever sleeps at the edge freezes by morning.
ev.chn_m_camels.text: A caravan of camels laden with coal from the Western Hills files through the city gate. Bells jingle, and the drivers in sheepskin hats curse loud enough to hear three streets away.
ev.chn_m_printed_book.text: You were given a printed book - neat characters pressed from a carved wooden block. It smells of ink and paste. You traced the lines with your finger until the lamp burned out.
ev.chn_m_kite.text: In spring you flew a paper kite shaped like a swallow. The string snapped twice, but the third time the swallow climbed higher than the pagoda.
ev.chn_m_crickets.text: In a little clay pot lives your fighting cricket, the Black General. Today he beat the neighbour’s champion - and you strutted about all evening.
ev.chn_m_silkworms.text: In spring you feed the silkworms mulberry leaves day and night. They munch so loudly it sounds like rain. No noise, no frying fish nearby - silkworms are fussy creatures.
ev.chn_m_rice_planting.text: All day you stand knee-deep in water planting rice seedlings, bunch after bunch, row after row. By evening your back won’t straighten, but the field lies green and even as embroidery.
ev.chn_m_dragon_pump.text: In the drought you and the neighbours take turns treading the square-pallet pump - the “dragon’s backbone”. Water creeps up the wooden trough onto the field. Singing makes it easier.
ev.chn_m_footbinding.text: They have begun to bind your feet - the custom of “respectable” families, so that a girl will make a good match one day. Every step hurts, and you will never again run with the other children.
ev.chn_m_ancestor_tablet.text: Every morning incense is lit before the wooden tablets bearing the ancestors’ names. Today you were trusted to set down a cup of tea and bow low - and you didn’t drop the cup.
ev.chn_m_calligraphy.text: The teacher makes you write the character for “eternity” a hundred times: it holds all eight basic brushstrokes. On the hundredth try he nodded. Once.
ev.chn_m_zaju.text: On the stage they are playing Judge Bao unmasking a villain, and the crowd shouts and throws coins. The actor with the painted face sang so well it sent shivers down your spine.
ev.chn_m_shadow_puppets.text: In the evening there was a shadow play behind a paper screen: leather puppets fought with swords, horses galloped, and one general lost his head and, to roars of laughter, found it again.
ev.chn_m_congee.text: In the hungry spring, thin rice gruel is handed out at the monastery gate. The queue stretches all the way to the bridge. You stood in it from dawn and got your bowl.
ev.chn_m_bride_chair.text: A red bridal sedan chair is carried down the street behind pipes and drums. The bride can’t be seen - only the edge of an embroidered veil. The neighbour women whisper about how many dowry chests she has.
ev.chn_m_fortune_teller.text: The fortune-teller on the corner studied your face and palm for a long time, then pronounced: “Lucky eyebrows, but the ears let you down.” And you had to pay for that.
ev.chn_m_blue_white.text: There is a new bowl on the table - white, with blue dragons. They say the blue pigment comes from distant Persia, and such bowls are fired at Jingdezhen, where the kilns smoke day and night.
ev.chn_m_abacus.text: You are learning the abacus: the beads click, and the shop clerk wants your fingers to fly faster than your tongue. “A merchant without an abacus is a boat without an oar.”
ev.chn_m_temple_fair.text: At the temple fair you can barely move: tightrope walkers, fire-eaters, sweet-sellers, and incense smoke so thick your eyes water.
ev.chn_m_grand_canal.text: Government rice barges for the capital move in a long line down the Grand Canal. Trackers haul them on towropes, singing, and the lock-keepers argue with every captain.
ev.chn_m_song_tea.text: You have been taught to make tea properly: green powder whisked with a bamboo whisk in a dark bowl until white froth rises. The longer the froth lasts, the more skilled the host.
ev.chn_m_ming_tea.text: Tea is no longer ground to powder but steeped as whole leaves in the cup - the custom since the first Ming emperor’s decree. The leaves unfurl in the hot water and the room smells of a spring mountainside.
ev.chn_m_frozen_canal.text: In winter the canal froze over, and boys go sledding on the ice. Chestnut roasters warm their hands over braziers and call out to passers-by.
ev.chn_m_temple_bell.text: At dawn the great bell of the hillside monastery sounds. They say it is heard even in the underworld, and for a moment the sinners there feel some relief.
ev.chn_m_luoyang_bridge.text: You walked across the Luoyang Bridge - a long stone bridge over the river mouth. They say the builders bred oysters on its piers so their shells would bind the stones tighter than mortar.
ev.chn_m_kitchen_god.text: Before New Year the paper Kitchen God’s lips are smeared with sweet syrup and the picture is burned - so that up in heaven he will say only sweet things about the household.
ev.chn_m_quanzhou_temples.text: On a single street stand a mosque with a stone arch, the Kaiyuan monastery with its twin pagodas, and the Tamil merchants’ temple with many-armed gods. Quanzhou prays in ten languages.
ev.chn_m_brocade.text: Weavers rinse brocade in the Jinjiang - the “Brocade River”. They say only its water makes silk dyes glow so brightly.
ev.chn_d_clan_school.title: The clan school
ev.chn_d_clan_school.text: The clan elders have opened a school at the ancestral hall: the teacher is paid from the clan’s charitable fields, and poor relations’ children study for free. But at home every pair of hands counts.
ev.chn_d_clan_school_later.title: A debt to the clan
ev.chn_d_clan_school_later.text: The clan remembers you: the elders who paid for your schooling ask you to draft a petition to the county office about a disputed field. It will take long, and no one mentions payment.
ev.chn_d_grain_tax.title: The big measure
ev.chn_d_grain_tax.text: The tax collector measures your grain with a “big dou” - a measure noticeably larger than the official one. The surplus will, of course, end up in his own granary.
ev.chn_d_grain_tax.complain.success: The magistrate ordered the measure checked. The collector went pale and poured the grain back.
ev.chn_d_grain_tax.complain.failure: The complaint was shelved, and the collector remembered you. Next time he took even more.
ev.chn_d_grain_tax.bribe: Slip the collector a string of cash
ev.chn_d_lijia.title: Head of the lijia
ev.chn_d_lijia.text: This year it is your household’s turn to head the lijia: to collect taxes from ten families and answer for every arrear with your own property.
ev.chn_d_lijia.note: The lijia system, set up under the Hongwu emperor in 1381, grouped villages into units of 110 households; wealthier households took turns collecting taxes and were liable for shortfalls. Many were ruined by the duty.
ev.chn_d_lijia.serve.success: The year passed without arrears. Neighbours bow to you in the street.
ev.chn_d_lijia.serve.failure: Two households couldn’t pay, and the shortfall was taken from you.
ev.chn_d_green_sprouts.title: “Green sprouts”
ev.chn_d_green_sprouts.text: The county has announced that under a new law the treasury will lend farmers grain and cash in spring, to be repaid at harvest. The interest is steep, but the moneylender charges more.
ev.chn_d_green_sprouts.note: The Green Sprouts law (1069) was part of Wang Anshi’s New Policies. In practice officials often forced the loans on farmers and collected them harshly.
ev.chn_d_green_sprouts_later.title: Time to repay
ev.chn_d_green_sprouts_later.text: The government loan has fallen due. The harvest was middling, but the official wants everything at once, with interest.
ev.chn_d_green_sprouts_later.beg.success: The official relented and took half for now.
ev.chn_d_green_sprouts_later.beg.failure: You got more time - at new interest. Now you are in debt.
ev.chn_d_funeral_loan.title: A funeral on credit
ev.chn_d_funeral_loan.text: {npc} asks for a loan to bury a relative. Without monks, musicians and a meal for the whole street the shame will last for years - and there is no money.
ev.chn_d_funeral_loan_later.title: A debt repaid
ev.chn_d_funeral_loan_later.text: {npc} has repaid the funeral loan - with interest and a box of moon cakes: “You saved my face back then.”
ev.chn_d_father_ill.title: Filial duty
ev.chn_d_father_ill.text: {npc}, your father, has taken to his bed. The physician speaks of a costly ginseng remedy, and the neighbours remind you that a filial child stays by the bedside day and night.
ev.chn_d_paper_money.title: Paper losing value
ev.chn_d_paper_money.text: Yuan paper money loses value month by month: a sack of rice now costs a wad of notes as thick as a finger. Your savings are in paper.
ev.chn_d_paper_money.convert: Buy silver and rice while you can
ev.chn_d_paper_money.keep: Wait for the treasury to restore order
ev.chn_d_paper_money.keep.success: You managed to pay off your debts in paper before it became worthless.
ev.chn_d_paper_money.keep.failure: Order never came. The notes are now good only for kindling.
ev.chn_d_gambling.title: The back room
ev.chn_d_gambling.text: In the back room of the teahouse they are throwing dice and betting on crickets. A friend tugs your sleeve: “Just one round, for luck!”
ev.chn_d_gambling.play.success: The dice fell your way. You left with a full purse - and a wish to come back.
ev.chn_d_gambling.play.failure: Luck turned away. You lost a month’s earnings.
ev.chn_d_adopt_heir.title: Who will carry on the line
ev.chn_d_adopt_heir.text: Many years have passed, and there is still no heir to make offerings to the ancestors. The relatives suggest adopting a nephew - many families do.
ev.chn_d_adopt_heir.temple: Pray to Guanyin for a child
ev.chn_d_concubine.title: A concubine
ev.chn_d_concubine.text: The relatives insist that a great house needs a concubine: more children, more hands, more prestige. {npc} says nothing, but the look says it all.
ev.chn_d_widow.title: A widow’s fidelity
ev.chn_d_widow.text: Your late husband’s family insists that a virtuous widow never remarries. The authorities even raise arches to honour “chaste widows”. And the matchmaker has called twice already.
ev.chn_d_widow_arch.title: An arch of chastity
ev.chn_d_widow_arch.text: At the county elders’ request a stone arch inscribed with your widow’s virtue has been raised in your honour. Passers-by bow to it. The nights are no warmer for it, but your name will outlive you.
ev.chn_d_bandits.title: Men from the hills
ev.chn_d_bandits.text: “Noble outlaws” have appeared in the hills: they rob the rich and the officials and, people say, give to the poor. An acquaintance urges you to join them - better than breaking your back for a landlord.
ev.chn_d_bandits.report.success: The county paid a reward. No one saw the acquaintance again.
ev.chn_d_bandits.report.failure: The outlaws learned who informed. They waylaid you by the well.
ev.chn_d_bandits_amnesty.title: The call to submit
ev.chn_d_bandits_amnesty.text: The authorities have proclaimed an amnesty: outlaws who lay down their arms will be taken into the imperial army. That is how many tales of noble outlaws end.
ev.chn_d_bandits_amnesty.refuse.success: The band went deeper into the hills. The plunder was rich.
ev.chn_d_bandits_amnesty.refuse.failure: Troops surrounded the camp. You barely broke out, badly wounded.
ev.chn_d_lawsuit.title: The boundary stone
ev.chn_d_lawsuit.text: Your neighbour has moved the boundary stone a full pace onto your land. You could sue at the yamen, but as the saying goes: “The yamen gate faces south - don’t go in without money.”
ev.chn_d_lawsuit.songshi.success: The litigation master drafted such a plaint that the neighbour moved the stone back and paid for the insult.
ev.chn_d_lawsuit.songshi.failure: The neighbour paid the clerks more. The case drags on and the money drains away.
ev.chn_d_lawsuit.elders: Ask the clan elders to judge
ev.chn_d_lawsuit.elders.success: The elders judged fairly. The stone went back, and the neighbours made peace over tea.
ev.chn_d_lawsuit.elders.failure: The elders turned out to be the neighbour’s relatives.
ev.chn_d_lawsuit.yield: Give up the pace of land
ev.chn_d_buy_land.title: Land or the shop
ev.chn_d_buy_land.text: You have saved money. The old merchants advise: “Land neither burns nor drowns - buy fields and put the children to their books.” But in the shop money works faster.
ev.chn_d_buy_land.shop.success: The goods sold fast. The money came back with a profit.
ev.chn_d_buy_land.shop.failure: Prices fell and part of the stock went unsold.
ev.chn_d_buy_land_later.title: Among the gentry
ev.chn_d_buy_land_later.text: The fields bring a steady income, and the county now sees your house differently: you are invited to the local gentry’s gatherings - you, a tradesman only yesterday!
ev.chn_d_corvee.title: Corvée
ev.chn_d_corvee.text: The county is calling men for corvée: mending dikes and dredging canals. A month without wages, hard labour and thin soup.
ev.chn_d_corvee.hide.success: The headman didn’t find you - or pretended not to.
ev.chn_d_corvee.hide.failure: They found you, fined you and marched you off to work anyway.
ev.chn_d_salt_smugglers.title: Night visitors
ev.chn_d_salt_smugglers.text: At night men with sacks knock at your door: salt smugglers ask you to hide their goods till morning. Government salt is dear, theirs half the price. They pay well.
ev.chn_d_salt_smugglers.hide.success: By morning the sacks were gone, and a string of cash lay under the mat.
ev.chn_d_salt_smugglers.hide.failure: The salt patrol found the sacks. You had to buy them off.
ev.chn_d_salt_smugglers_later.title: Old acquaintances
ev.chn_d_salt_smugglers_later.text: The same smugglers are at your door again. Their leader has grown rich and offers you a share in the business - while reminding you that you have helped them before.
ev.chn_d_salt_smugglers_later.join.succe: The salt flowed, and so did the silver.
ev.chn_d_salt_smugglers_later.join.failu: The salt patrol caught the whole gang. You were branded a criminal and lost half of everything.
ev.chn_d_salt_smugglers_later.refuse.suc: The leader shrugged and left. They never came back.
ev.chn_d_salt_smugglers_later.refuse.fai: They didn’t forgive the refusal: a week later you were beaten in an alley.
ev.chn_d_temple_stele.title: A name in stone
ev.chn_d_temple_stele.text: Money is being collected to repair the old temple. The names of the biggest donors will be carved on a stone stele by the entrance - for ever.
ev.chn_d_temple_stele_later.title: The stele by the temple
ev.chn_d_temple_stele_later.text: Years have passed, and people still read your name on the stele aloud. Today a stranger bowed to you in the street: “Are you the one who paid for the new beams?”
ev.chn_d_arab_partner.title: A partner from the land of the Dashi
ev.chn_d_arab_partner.text: An Arab merchant is looking for a partner: to fit out a junk with silk and porcelain for Java, and perhaps the Persian Gulf. She will be back in two years or so - or never.
ev.chn_d_arab_partner_later.title: News of the junk
ev.chn_d_arab_partner_later.text: The junk still hasn’t come. Another merchant offers to buy your share - for less than you put in, but for certain.
ev.chn_d_arab_partner_later.wait.success: One morning your junk sailed into harbour, laden with pepper, frankincense and pearls. Your partner kept his word.
ev.chn_d_arab_partner_later.wait.failure: Word came: the junk was wrecked off the coast of Champa. Your partner went down with her.
ev.chn_d_child_fever.title: Fever
ev.chn_d_child_fever.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} has been burning with fever for three days. A neighbour says to call a Daoist to drive out the evil spirit; the physician at the market charges dearly for his decoctions.
ev.chn_d_child_fever.daoist.success: The Daoist chanted and burned paper talismans, and by morning the fever broke.
ev.chn_d_child_fever.daoist.failure: The talismans didn’t help. The illness passed on its own - slowly and hard.
ev.chn_d_child_fever.physician.success: The physician read the pulse, gave a bitter decoction - and two days later the child asked for food.
ev.chn_d_child_fever.physician.failure: The decoctions didn’t help. The child recovered, but stayed weak for a long time.
ev.chn_d_child_fever.home.success: Cool cloths and herbal tea did their work.
ev.chn_d_child_fever.home.failure: You didn’t sleep for a week. It turned out all right, but the fear stayed for years.
ev.chn_f_convert.title: The name of Amitabha
ev.chn_f_convert.text: After a hard year you keep returning to the monastery. An old monk says suffering is born of attachment and teaches you to repeat the name of Amitabha, lord of the Pure Land.
ev.chn_f_convert.both: Honour both the ancestors and the Buddha, like many do
ev.chn_f_ordination.title: Taking the tonsure
ev.chn_f_ordination.text: The abbot offers you ordination. Without an official certificate - a dudie - you cannot become a monastic, and it is costly, but the community is willing to help.
ev.chn_f_ordination.ordain: Shave your head and enter the monastery
ev.chn_f_pilgrimage.title: The sacred mountain
ev.chn_f_pilgrimage.text: The monks say a pilgrimage to a sacred mountain - Emei, Wutai or Putuo island - washes away the sins of past lives. The road is long, over passes haunted by monkeys and bandits.
ev.chn_f_pilgrimage.text.chengdu: The monks say a pilgrimage to Mount Emei - close by, two weeks’ walk - washes away the sins of past lives. At the summit, they say, you can see the Buddha’s Light in the clouds.
ev.chn_f_pilgrimage.go.success: At the summit you saw a rainbow halo in the clouds. You came home a different person.
ev.chn_f_pilgrimage.go.failure: On the pass you slipped off the trail and spent a long time healing in a mountain monastery.
ev.chn_f_white_lotus.title: The White Lotus
ev.chn_f_white_lotus.text: The neighbours whisper of the White Lotus: Maitreya the future Buddha will soon descend, the old world will fall, and the last shall be first. The meetings are secret - they carry the death penalty.
ev.chn_f_white_lotus.note: The White Lotus teaching was a popular Buddhist movement awaiting Maitreya. Both the Yuan and the Ming banned it; the Red Turbans rose under its banner in 1351.
ev.chn_f_white_lotus_later.title: Denounced
ev.chn_f_white_lotus_later.text: Guards came at dawn: someone has informed on the White Lotus meetings. They are reading out names - and yours is among them.
ev.chn_f_white_lotus_later.deny.success: They believed you - or couldn’t be bothered.
ev.chn_f_white_lotus_later.deny.failure: You were taken to the yamen. You got back only months later, with an empty purse.
ev.chn_f_elixir.title: The pill of immortality
ev.chn_f_elixir.text: A Daoist alchemist offers a pill of immortality made from cinnabar and other secret substances. He swears an old minister took them and lived to ninety.
ev.chn_f_elixir.take.success: Nothing happened - except you felt livelier. Perhaps from faith alone.
ev.chn_f_elixir.take.failure: Your stomach cramped and your hands began to shake. Mercury pills do not make you immortal.
ev.chn_f_ancestral_rite.title: Offerings to the ancestors
ev.chn_f_ancestral_rite.text: It is time for the great sacrifice in the ancestral hall. You can make it lavish - with musicians and a whole pig - or follow Zhu Xi’s Family Rituals: modest and strict.
ev.chn_f_ancestral_rite.lavish: Lavishly, for the whole county to see
ev.chn_f_jesuit.title: The scholar from the West
ev.chn_f_jesuit.text: A Western scholar dressed as a Confucian shows his guests a striking clock, a map of the whole world and books about the Lord of Heaven. Some officials, they say, have already taken up his faith.
ev.chn_f_jesuit.note: The Jesuit Matteo Ricci lived in Beijing from 1601. His disciples, the scholars Xu Guangqi and Li Zhizao, became Christians and translated European mathematics with him.
ev.chn_f_jesuit.leave: Look at the clock and leave
ev.chn_f_synagogue.title: The new synagogue
ev.chn_f_synagogue.text: The community has consecrated a new synagogue by the Earth Market. Jews here are called “those who pluck out the sinew”, for their custom of not eating the sciatic nerve. Your teacher advises: if you want to get on, study the Confucian classics, not the Torah.
ev.chn_f_synagogue.note: The Kaifeng synagogue was built in 1163. The Jewish community, probably from Persia, survived until the nineteenth century, gradually adopting Chinese language and customs; many members passed the examinations and held office.
ev.chn_f_synagogue.torah: Hold to the faith of your forebears
ev.chn_f_pu_name.title: Two names
ev.chn_f_pu_name.text: After Friday prayers at the Qingjing mosque, an old merchant advises: “Take a Chinese surname - Pu, say - and learn the characters; officials are easier to deal with that way.” The imam frowns.
ev.chn_mv_capital.title: To the capital
ev.chn_mv_capital.text: A fellow villager has come back from the capital - {capital} - in a silk robe: “There’s work for everyone there, and the pay is double. Come with me!”
ev.chn_mv_port.title: The city of foreign ships
ev.chn_mv_port.text: Merchants talk of Quanzhou: hundreds of foreign ships in the harbour, ten languages spoken in the streets, and any clever man can grow rich there.
ev.chn_mv_sichuan.title: The empty lands of Sichuan
ev.chn_mv_sichuan.text: The authorities are calling settlers to Sichuan, emptied by the wars: land, seed and several years free of tax. The road leads over the mountains, and there is no coming back.
ev.chn_mv_sichuan.note: In the early Ming, Sichuan, devastated by the wars at the end of the Yuan, was resettled with migrants from Huguang and other provinces.
ev.chn_mv_yongle.title: The resettlement decree
ev.chn_mv_yongle.text: An edict of the Yongle emperor: wealthy families from the south are to move to the new capital in the north, Beijing. Refusal is not an option. Buying your way out might work, but it will cost dearly.
ev.chn_mv_yongle.note: Preparing to move the capital to Beijing, the Yongle emperor (1402–1424) relocated thousands of wealthy households there from Jiangnan and Shanxi.
ev.chn_t_exam_accused.title: A false accusation
ev.chn_t_exam_accused.text: You are accused of smuggling a crib into the examination hall in your sleeve - a silk scrap covered in tiny characters. You are innocent, but the informer is an influential man’s son, and his word weighs more.
ev.chn_t_exam_accused.fight.success: The examiners compared the handwriting and declared the accusation false. Your firmness became the talk of the capital.
ev.chn_t_exam_accused.fight.failure: They didn’t believe you. Your name was struck from the lists, and the examinations are closed to you.
ev.chn_t_exam_accused.bribe: Pay to have it hushed up
ev.chn_t_mongol_capture.title: The Mongols in the city
ev.chn_t_mongol_capture.text: A Mongol detachment has burst into the city. Captives are herded into the square and sorted: craftsmen to one side, to be taken away to work for the khans. The rest face an unknown fate.
ev.chn_t_mongol_capture.craft.success: You showed your hands and answered their questions. You were enrolled in an artisan household - alive, but without home or goods.
ev.chn_t_mongol_capture.craft.failure: The lie was discovered. You were led off with the other captives - into bondage.
ev.chn_t_mongol_capture.hide.success: You spent two days in the dark. The detachment moved on, leaving ashes behind.
ev.chn_t_mongol_capture.hide.failure: They found you. Captives were given no mercy.
ev.chn_t_wokou.title: Wokou raiders
ev.chn_t_wokou.text: The wokou have come from the sea - “Japanese pirates”, though most of them are local smugglers. Warehouses are burning and people are running for the hills.
ev.chn_t_wokou.fight.success: With the neighbours you held them off at the bridge. The pirates went in search of easier prey.
ev.chn_t_wokou.fight.failure: You were badly wounded in the fight.
ev.chn_t_wokou.flee: Flee with what you can carry
ev.chn_t_wokou.join: Go to sea with the pirates
ev.chn_t_treasure.title: A jar in the earth
ev.chn_t_treasure.text: Your hoe struck something hard. In the earth lies a clay jar filled to the brim with old copper coins from Tang times.
ev.chn_t_treasure.keep.success: You exchanged the coins bit by bit with money-changers in different towns. Nobody suspected anything.
ev.chn_t_treasure.keep.failure: Word reached the landlord, and you had to hand over most of the hoard.
ev.chn_t_famine.title: The hungry year
ev.chn_t_famine.text: The harvest has failed for the second year. The grain is gone, the elm bark already stripped. A broker offers to sell you into service in a rich house: you’ll be fed, and your family will get a little silver.
ev.chn_t_famine.flee: Leave to look for food elsewhere
ev.chn_t_famine.endure: Hold out till the next harvest
ev.chn_t_famine.endure.success: You lived to spring on bran and wild greens.
ev.chn_t_famine.endure.failure: Hunger wore you down. You can barely stand.
ev.chn_t_palace_selection.title: Selection for the palace
ev.chn_t_palace_selection.text: Eunuchs have arrived from the capital to select girls for the palace. The district is in a panic: families are marrying their girls off to the first man they find, rather than give them up.
ev.chn_t_palace_selection.hide.failure: They found you and took you to the capital.
ev.chn_t_palace_release.title: Released from the palace
ev.chn_t_palace_release.text: After long years of service in the inner quarters you have been released from the palace with a small gift. You know palace etiquette, can sew and read - and you are free again.
ev.chn_t_eunuch_patron.title: A eunuch’s favour
ev.chn_t_eunuch_patron.text: A powerful palace eunuch has noticed you and offers his patronage: contracts, posts, gifts. In return - loyalty, and small services that are best not asked about.
ev.chn_t_eunuch_fall.title: The patron falls
ev.chn_t_eunuch_fall.text: Your eunuch patron has fallen: a purge has begun at court. Everyone who took his gifts is being summoned for questioning.
ev.chn_t_eunuch_fall.deny.success: They forgot about you - there were bigger fish to catch.
ev.chn_t_eunuch_fall.deny.failure: Letters turned up. You were thrown in prison and stripped of almost everything.
ev.chn_t_junk_return.title: A junk from the Southern Seas
ev.chn_t_junk_return.text: The junk you put your last money into with three partners has returned from the Southern Seas - with pepper, sandalwood and ivory. The port customs is already waiting for its share.
ev.chn_t_junk_return.smuggle: Unload at night past the customs
ev.chn_t_junk_return.smuggle.success: The goods were with the buyers before dawn. An unheard-of profit.
ev.chn_t_junk_return.smuggle.failure: The guards were waiting at the jetty. The cargo was seized and you were locked up.
ev.chn_t_land_seized.title: Someone else’s deeds
ev.chn_t_land_seized.text: A powerful county family has declared your plot their own. They have deeds with seals; you have only your grandfather’s word.
ev.chn_t_land_seized.court.success: An old tax register with your name turned up. The magistrate didn’t dare argue with the record.
ev.chn_t_land_seized.court.failure: The court sided with the powerful. You lost both the land and the money spent on the case.
ev.chn_t_city_fire.title: Fire!
ev.chn_t_city_fire.text: The gong sounds in the night: fire! The wind drives the flames through the wooden quarters faster than people can run. Firemen with hooks and buckets are already pulling down neighbouring houses.
ev.chn_t_city_fire.save_goods.success: You carried out the chest and the account books. The house burned, but what matters survived.
ev.chn_t_city_fire.save_goods.failure: A beam crashed down right in front of you. You got out burned and with almost nothing.
ev.chn_t_city_fire.help: Help the neighbours get the children out
ev.chn_t_inheritance.title: A shop by the harbour
ev.chn_t_inheritance.text: A letter has come from Quanzhou: a distant relative, a trader, has died and left you a shop by the harbour. To claim it, you must go in person.
ev.chn_t_inheritance.sell: Sell the shop through an agent
ev.chn_t_master_ruined.title: The master is ruined
ev.chn_t_master_ruined.text: The master’s house has collapsed: debts, a lawsuit, the master himself has fled. The steward is selling off the servants, and in the confusion the box of bond deeds stands unguarded.
ev.chn_t_master_ruined.burn: Find your deed and burn it
ev.chn_t_master_ruined.burn.success: The deed burned in the hearth. No one can prove you belong to anyone.
ev.chn_t_master_ruined.burn.failure: The steward caught you at the box.
ev.chn_t_master_ruined.buy: Buy yourself out with your savings
ev.chn_j_exam_prefecture.title: The prefectural examinations
ev.chn_j_exam_prefecture.text: The prefectural examinations have begun: three days locked in a cramped cell, an essay on a theme from Mencius and verses by strict rules. Of every hundred candidates only a few will pass.
ev.chn_j_exam_prefecture.honest.success: Your name is on the yellow list at the gate! You are a juren, “a recommended man”, and may go on to the metropolitan examinations.
ev.chn_j_exam_prefecture.honest.failure: Your name is not on the list. Another three years over the books.
ev.chn_j_exam_prefecture.crib: Smuggle in a crib in your sleeve
ev.chn_j_exam_prefecture.crib.success: No one noticed. Your name is on the list.
ev.chn_j_exam_prefecture.crib.failure: A guard searched you at the entrance. Disgrace, and a ban from the examinations.
ev.chn_j_exam_prefecture.skip: Skip this round and prepare better
ev.chn_j_exam_capital.title: The metropolitan examinations
ev.chn_j_exam_capital.text: In the capital the metropolitan examinations are held, followed by the palace examination, where the emperor himself sets the questions. Of thousands of candidates, a few hundred will become jinshi.
ev.chn_j_exam_capital.sit.success: You are a jinshi! You have been given an official post, and back home the villagers are already hanging a plaque on your gate.
ev.chn_j_exam_capital.sit.failure: Failure. You stand before the list and can’t find your name at the top or at the bottom.
ev.chn_j_exam_old.title: The eternal candidate
ev.chn_j_exam_old.text: You are past thirty-five and still without a degree. In the village they snigger: “The eternal candidate.” A rich family wants you to tutor their children for good money, and the county office needs a clerk.
ev.chn_j_monk_pawn.title: The Inexhaustible Treasury
ev.chn_j_monk_pawn.text: The monastery runs a pawnshop - the “Inexhaustible Treasury”. A farmer wants a loan against his padded quilt. Clearly he will never be able to repay.
ev.chn_j_monk_certificate.title: The government certificate
ev.chn_j_monk_certificate.text: The treasury is selling ordination certificates again. Without one you are an “unregistered” monastic, and any inspection could return you to lay life and the tax rolls.
ev.chn_j_monk_certificate.risk.failure: The inspectors sent you back to lay life. You had to hire on as a porter.
ev.chn_j_tea_monopoly.title: The government tea bureau
ev.chn_j_tea_monopoly.text: The government tea bureau buys the harvest at its own price - a third of what private merchants offer. And selling privately is strictly forbidden.
ev.chn_j_tea_monopoly.smuggle: Sell to merchants on the sly
ev.chn_j_tea_monopoly.smuggle.success: The merchant took the baskets at night and paid in silver.
ev.chn_j_tea_monopoly.smuggle.failure: The tea patrol intercepted the porters on the pass.
ev.chn_j_tea_contest.title: The tea contest
ev.chn_j_tea_contest.text: The town is holding a tea contest: the powder is whisked and judges watch whose froth is whitest and clings longest to the bowl. The winner sells the harvest at triple the price.
ev.chn_j_tea_contest.enter.success: Your froth lasted longest. Merchants queued up for your tea.
ev.chn_j_tea_contest.enter.failure: Your froth sank faster than your neighbour’s. All you got was the cost of the journey.
ev.chn_j_kiln_firing.title: The dragon kiln
ev.chn_j_kiln_firing.text: The dragon kiln on the hillside is loaded with a thousand pieces. For three days and nights the heat must be held steady - one slip and it all turns to shards.
ev.chn_j_kiln_firing.watch: Stay awake at the firebox yourself
ev.chn_j_kiln_firing.watch.success: The kiln cooled, and out came even, ringing bowls.
ev.chn_j_kiln_firing.watch.failure: Towards dawn you dozed off. Half the pieces cracked.
ev.chn_j_kiln_firing.hire.success: The old man knew his business.
ev.chn_j_kiln_firing.hire.failure: The hired man got drunk on the second day.
ev.chn_j_kiln_crackle.title: Crackle
ev.chn_j_kiln_crackle.text: The glaze on a whole batch of bowls has crazed into a web of fine cracks. A flaw? But a dealer from the capital insists that noble connoisseurs are looking for exactly this.
ev.chn_j_kiln_crackle.sell_art: Sell it as a new style
ev.chn_j_kiln_crackle.sell_art.success: The connoisseurs called it “fish scale” and paid triple.
ev.chn_j_kiln_crackle.sell_art.failure: The dealer beat the price down to that of shards.
ev.chn_j_kiln_crackle.smash: Smash the flawed ware, as a master’s honour demands
ev.chn_j_kiln_own.title: A kiln of your own
ev.chn_j_kiln_own.text: An old master is retiring and offers to sell you his kiln, together with his apprentices and customers.
ev.chn_j_salt_frontier.title: Grain for salt
ev.chn_j_salt_frontier.text: Under the kaizhong system a salt certificate goes to whoever delivers grain to the garrisons on the northern frontier. The road is long, and the nomads are near.
ev.chn_j_salt_frontier.go: Haul the grain to the frontier yourself
ev.chn_j_salt_frontier.go.success: The grain is delivered, the certificate in hand. Lianghuai salt will turn into silver.
ev.chn_j_salt_frontier.go.failure: The convoy was attacked. You came back wounded, with empty carts.
ev.chn_j_salt_inspector.title: The salt inspector
ev.chn_j_salt_inspector.text: The salt inspector hints that without a gift your certificates will lie on his desk until next year.
ev.chn_j_salt_inspector.refuse.success: The inspector was replaced, and his successor signed everything that day.
ev.chn_j_salt_inspector.refuse.failure: The certificates lay there for a year. Salt prices fell; the losses were huge.
ev.chn_j_salt_inspector.complain.success: The censor took up the case. Now the inspector bows to you first.
ev.chn_j_salt_inspector.complain.failure: The censor turned out to be the inspector’s friend.
ev.chn_j_story_official.title: The tale of the greedy magistrate
ev.chn_j_story_official.text: The crowd at the pleasure ground demands the tale of the greedy magistrate. Everyone knows whom you’ll be playing - and he himself is sitting in the third row.
ev.chn_j_story_official.bold.success: The hall laughed till it cried, and the magistrate laughed loudest of all - so nobody would think it was about him.
ev.chn_j_story_official.bold.failure: That evening his servants waylaid you.
ev.chn_j_story_official.safe: Tell of the Three Kingdoms instead
ev.chn_j_story_official.flatter: Make up a hymn to the wise magistrate
ev.chn_j_story_book.title: A picture book
ev.chn_j_story_book.text: A bookseller from Jianyang wants to write down your tales and print them with pictures across the top of each page. He pays at once - but your name won’t be on the book.
ev.chn_j_story_book.refuse: A tale lives only in the voice
ev.chn_j_canal_lock.title: The queue at the lock
ev.chn_j_canal_lock.text: A hundred barges wait at the lock. The keeper lets through first those who “bow” with silver, and your rice may get damp.
ev.chn_j_canal_lock.wait.success: The weather held, and the rice arrived dry.
ev.chn_j_canal_lock.wait.failure: The rains came, and part of the cargo was spoiled.
ev.chn_j_canal_lock.push.failure: The boatmen from the other barges gave you a beating.
ev.chn_j_junk_voyage.title: To the Southern Seas
ev.chn_j_junk_voyage.text: The captain of a big junk is hiring crew for a voyage to Malacca. Pay up front; back in a year with a profit - or not at all.
ev.chn_j_junk_voyage.go.success: You saw foreign shores and came home with silver and stories.
ev.chn_j_junk_voyage.go.failure: A typhoon battered the junk. You came home sick and with no earnings.
ev.chn_j_own_boat.title: A boat of your own
ev.chn_j_own_boat.text: The owner of several barges is getting old and is willing to sell you one in instalments.
ev.chn_j_flying_plots.title: Flying plots
ev.chn_j_flying_plots.text: A landlord asks you to “correct” the land registers: to enter part of his fields under poor neighbours’ names so that they pay the tax. It’s called “flying plots”. He pays generously.
ev.chn_j_flying_plots.report.success: The magistrate punished the landlord and remembered your name.
ev.chn_j_flying_plots.report.failure: The landlord and the magistrate turned out to be old friends. You were fined for slander.
ev.chn_j_flying_plots_later.title: The land survey
ev.chn_j_flying_plots_later.text: Officials have arrived to remeasure the fields, and the “flying plots” are surfacing one after another. Your handwriting in the old registers is instantly recognisable.
ev.chn_j_flying_plots_later.blame: Put the blame on the landlord
ev.chn_j_flying_plots_later.blame.succes: They believed the landlord less than you.
ev.chn_j_flying_plots_later.blame.failur: The landlord produced your receipt. You were thrown in jail.
ev.chn_j_clerk_promotion.title: A recommendation
ev.chn_j_clerk_promotion.text: The magistrate values your precision and is willing to recommend you for office - without the examinations. All it takes is gifts for the right people.
ev.chn_j_military_household.title: A military household
ev.chn_j_military_household.text: You belong to a military household: service is hereditary, and your descendants will be soldiers too. An officer offers a transfer to the northern frontier - double rations, but cold and nomads.
ev.chn_j_military_household.go.success: You served your term on the Wall and came back with a reward.
ev.chn_j_military_household.go.failure: An arrow hit you in a skirmish with the nomads.
ev.chn_j_military_household.desert.succe: You went to another province under a false name.
ev.chn_j_military_household.desert.failu: You were caught and flogged in front of the ranks.
ev.chn_j_hold_gate.title: Who held the gate
ev.chn_j_hold_gate.text: After the skirmish with the raiders, the commander asks who held the gate. Everyone looks at you.
ev.chn_j_physician_prefect.title: A patient in the prefect’s house
ev.chn_j_physician_prefect.text: You have been called to the aged lady of the prefect’s household. The previous physicians were all thrown out in disgrace - one, they say, was beaten.
ev.chn_j_physician_prefect.treat.success: A month later the old lady was out of bed. The prefect sent you silk and a plaque reading “Hand of Mercy”.
ev.chn_j_physician_prefect.treat.failure: There was no improvement, and you too were shown the gate.
